verdict.rationale: Bugbot lets teams write project-specific review guidelines in `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`, and admins can create organization-wide rules in Bugbot Automations. These rules are applied in automatic reviews on every PR update, and a verbose mode lists which rules were loaded. However, the evidence frames these as review guidance that produces comments, not as discrete agentic pre-merge checks with pass/fail status. Missing for 10: documented pass/fail check results or merge gating, examples of plain-language rules like 'docs updated' or 'tests cover new paths', and hands-on corroboration that custom rules are enforced reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I define custom agentic pre-merge checks in plain language — 'docs updated', 'tests cover new paths' — that run on every PR

citations.quote: Create `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` files in your repository to give Bugbot project-specific review guidelines.
Team admins can also create organization-wide rules in [Bugbot Automations](https://cursor.com/automations/from-cursor/bugbot).
Runs automatic reviews on every PR update
Bugbot replies with a table of the rules included in that review
